units.title: The actual OU half-refresh and its corrected moment budget
units.boundary: This is only Algorithm 3.1's first partial momentum refresh and the adapter needed before the existing two-layer Picard moment theorem. It does not construct the repeated phase history, prove the run-wide state estimate, instantiate the Picard Gaussian array, prove the numerical D.7 bound, aggregate D.8, or prove Theorem 5.1.

sources.label: Chen–Chewi–Lu–Zhang, Algorithm 3.1
sources.scope: First partial momentum refresh at lines 282–300, used in the proof of Lemma D.4 at lines 2177–2180.

assumptions: The incoming phase-state law nu on E×E is a probability measure, and the combined square ‖X−x*‖²+‖Pinit‖² is integrable with expectation at most M.
E is a complete finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space and h≥0.
Freshness of Z~N(0,I) is represented by the actual product measure nu⊗stdGaussian(E), rather than by assuming the mixed term has expectation zero.
units.statement: Set a=exp(−h/2), sigma=sqrt(1−exp(−h)), X0=X and P0=a Pinit+sigma Z on the product law of the incoming state and a fresh standard Gaussian. Then X0 and P0 are measurable, their combined squared distance is integrable, and its expectation satisfies the exact identity and corrected budget below.

steps.title: Realize the fresh draw by a product law
steps.text: A sample is a pair ((X,Pinit),Z) distributed according to nu⊗gamma_d. The first coordinate is the incoming phase state and the second is a genuinely fresh standard Gaussian. Coordinate projections and continuous linear combinations make X0 and P0 measurable.
steps.lean: The public X and P0 lets use product projections; the final fun_prop goals prove their measurability.

steps.title: Establish every integrability premise
steps.text: Nonnegativity lets us extract the position and momentum square integrability from the combined incoming energy. L2 then gives integrability of Pinit itself. The shared ASTIS theorem gives ‖Z‖² in L1, while Mathlib's Gaussian integrability API separately gives Z in L1; together these make the mixed inner product integrable on the product measure.
steps.formula: \|X-x_*\|^2,\|P_{\rm init}\|^2\in L^1(\nu),\quad P_{\rm init}\in L^1(\nu),\quad Z,\|Z\|^2\in L^1(\gamma_d).
steps.lean: hposI, hmomI, hmom1, hgaussI, hz1 and Integrable.op_fst_snd justify Fubini and all subsequent integral algebra.

steps.title: Use actual independence to kill the cross term
steps.text: For every fixed incoming momentum, the Gaussian mean is zero. Fubini is legal because the mixed inner product was proved integrable, hence its expectation under the product law vanishes without a centering assumption on Pinit.
steps.formula: \mathbb E_{\nu\otimes\gamma_d}\langle P_{\rm init},Z\rangle=\mathbb E_\nu\langle P_{\rm init},\mathbb E_{\gamma_d}Z\rangle=0.

steps.title: Expand the refreshed square
steps.text: The coefficients satisfy a²=e^(−h) and sigma²=1−e^(−h). Expanding the Hilbert norm, integrating the four integrable terms, using the zero cross term and E‖Z‖²=d gives the exact identity.
steps.lean: ha2, hs2, hexpand, hpieces and heq mirror this algebra and product integration.

steps.title: Derive the consumer-ready bound
steps.text: Because h≥0, 0<e^(−h)≤1. Replacing the damped momentum term by the incoming momentum square and applying the input budget yields M+(1−e^(−h))d. The extra dimension term must remain visible until the later paper-parameter absorption step.
steps.lean: hexp, hweighted and heq prove the final inequality. The focused test passes this result to picard_center_gradient_moment.

units.lean_statement: The source's independent Gaussian draw is represented definitionally by a product measure. The conclusion exposes measurability and integrability because the next Picard theorem requires them, and keeps Pinit distinct from the refreshed P0.
units.lean_proof: ASTIS supplies the canonical Gaussian norm-square leaf and the paper-specific product-law adapter. Mathlib supplies product Fubini, Gaussian mean/covariance, Lp-to-integrability and Hilbert norm algebra.
